To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

similitude can be achieved for SE(B) and C(T) specimens if the crack depth is at least 1/2 of the specimen's thickness, and for clamped SE(T), if the specimen's thickness is at least 2 times the ligament size.
the similitude limits of the J integral are a function of the crack length and the thickness for the SE(B) specimen, and of the crack depth and the thickness for both C(T) and SE(T).

The deformation limit M for the J integral is a material property that depends on the yield stress and the fracture toughness, but it also depends on the geometry of the structure or the specimen and the load ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a rational and consistent methodology to assess the validity of the J integral approach for the structural integrity assessment of pressure vessel and pipeline components.

establishing objective criteria for similitude in the one parameter framework, and the results obtained in this work can be used in the design of new experiments to obtain J R curves, in the validation of numerical models and in the assessment of the integrity of structural components.

the development of a methodology that enables the determination of the limits of validity of elastic plastic fracture mechanics based on Jc and J R curves, for the most common structural integrity applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the similitude of stress fields in the crack tip region is ensured when the following condition is met: M < 1.
the similitude condition M 0.5 is a safe criterion for assessing the validity limits of the one-parameter elastic plastic fracture mechanics framework.
the J integral can be applied to assess the fracture behavior of a structure with confidence, if the specimen is sufficiently large, i.e. the M value is greater or equal to one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the similitude criterion for the C(T) and SE(T), and for SE(B) with a = 2.5 T, can be established by the condition M < 1.5.
the similitude criterion is valid for all the geometries and loading modes considered in this work, as long as the M values are greater or equal to the critical values M c.
, in general terms, similitude can be ensured for a wide range of crack depths and specimen thicknesses for C(T) specimens and short crack depths in SE(B) and in clamped SE(T).
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when similitude is not ensured, the fracture mechanics assessment based on a one parameter approach may lead to unsafe predictions of the structural integrity.
the one parameter fracture toughness Jc is not valid for short cracked specimens and, therefore, should only be employed in the assessment of thick and long cracked structures.
the J integral is valid to describe the stress field ahead of the crack tip in C(T) specimens, provided that the thickness is at least 10 times larger than the ligament size.
